title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services

reading.body:
Scammers used AI-generated video and images to create fake social media profiles impersonating a real immigration attorney. The deployment failure was the absence of identity verification on social platforms, allowing hundreds of fraudulent accounts to operate across TikTok, Facebook, and Instagram before removal by a hired anti-piracy company. The scam targeted vulnerable immigrants seeking legal services, directing them through WhatsApp and payment apps to extract fees for services never provided.

This is impersonation enabled by generative AI. The criminals created deepfakes of a legitimate attorney to establish false credibility. What would have caught this earlier: identity verification requirements for legal service providers on social media, or platform monitoring for AI-generated video content used in financial fraud schemes.

It is not established whether the platforms had been notified before the anti-piracy company's intervention, or what measures the platforms subsequently implemented to prevent similar misuse.

reports.title: Scammers steal identity of renowned Miami attorney to target immigrants on social media
South Florida immigration attorney says AI scammers are using his identity to target immigrants
Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney

summary:
A South Florida immigration attorney is warning the public about AI-generated scams using his identity to defraud vulnerable immigrants. Angel Leal, who has practiced immigration law for more than 30 years, discovered that criminals created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI videos featuring his likeness. These fraudulent videos falsely offer immigration services such as US residency assistance in exchange for payments ranging up to $2,200. Leal first noticed the problem when potential clients began calling his office after seeing the fake content.

The scheme has grown significantly over recent months, prompting Leal to hire an anti-piracy company that removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles across multiple platforms, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The scams typically direct victims to contact numbers on WhatsApp and send fake contracts before requesting payment through apps like Venmo and Zelle. Leal plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the fraud and urges immigrants to verify anyone offering legal services online and avoid immediate payment requests on social media.
